problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V=\text{Col}(A)$ spanned by the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ of the matrix $A$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ shown above. Given that ${a}_{1}⊥{a}_{2},$ and that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
worked_solution:
Since the first two vectors are already orthogonal, we proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: We set ${v}_{2}={a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3**. Next, we find ${v}_{3}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{3}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-\frac{4}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{6}{10}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{3}{5}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{5} \\ -\frac{1}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\frac{a}{b}=\frac{(-\frac{2}{5})}{(-\frac{1}{5})}=2.
$$
